carrier: Course/author archive copy of the published ICFP 2000 article (Claessen & Hughes, 'QuickCheck: A Lightweight Tool for Random Testing of Haskell Programs'), 12 pages, ACM copyright block and ICFP '00 venue line on page 1, served by the Tufts CS257 reading archive; not a preprint and not the publisher's own bytes (DOI landing page dl.acm.org returned 403 from this host).
carrier_class: third-party mirror of the version of record
carrier_evidence: page 1 carries the ACM notice: `ICFP '00, Montreal, Canada.` / `Copyright 2000 ACM 1-58113-202-6/00/0009 .. 5.00` (quickcheck-icfp00-icfp-2000-course-copy.pdftotext.txt, page 1)
12 pages, matching Crossref `page: 268-279` for DOI 10.1145/351240.351266 (which also reports `content-version: vor`)
title page and ABSTRACT match the DOI record's title `QuickCheck` and the ICFP'00 venue
the carrier prints no proceedings folios: `grep -c '268\|279' <pdftotext>` = 0, so page numbers are taken from Crossref, not from the carrier
file was produced 2012-09-04 by dvipsk 5.58f / GPL Ghostscript 9.04 (pdfinfo), i.e. a re-rendered copy, not the 2000 typesetting
tier_reading: Tier A stands for the text: the bytes are the published article's text (VOR per Crossref), so §-level and quoted passages may be cited as the published article. Two caveats for citation hygiene: (i) the carrier is a third-party course mirror, so a sha256 pins this mirror's bytes, not the publisher's; (ii) printed proceedings page numbers (268-279) are not observable on the carrier and are inherited from the DOI/Crossref record, while the mirror's own davit-generated PDF page numbering is 1-12.

extraction.ligature_artifact: the Type1 fonts map ligatures onto missing glyphs: `fi`/`fl` vanish and leave a space (`de ne` = define, `classi es` = classifies, `speci cation` = specification); `ffi` arrives as control byte 0x0e (`ine\x0ecient` = inefficient, `di\x0eculty` = difficulty). Every quote below containing such a word was re-checked against the rendered page image (pdftoppm -r 200 -png) before being written with the true letters.

quotes.quote: Properties are described as Haskell functions, and can be automatically tested on random input
quotes.location: §Abstract, PDF page 1 (printed p. 268), left column, sentence 2 — words 14

quotes.quote: The function quickCheck takes a law as a parameter and applies it to a large number of randomly generated arguments
quotes.location: §2.1 A Simple Example, PDF page 2 (printed p. 269), left column, after the `OK: passed 100 tests.` transcript — words 20

quotes.quote: The best solution, though, is to replace the condition with a custom test data generator for ordered lists.
quotes.location: §2.4 Monitoring Test Data, PDF page 3 (printed p. 270), right column, opening sentence — words 18

quotes.quote: QuickCheck provides support for the programmer to define his or her own test data generators, with control over the distribution of test data
quotes.location: §2.4 Monitoring Test Data, PDF page 3 (printed p. 270), right column, penultimate paragraph (the `forAll orderedList` example precedes it) — words 23; `define` is rendered as the fi ligature (image-checked)

quotes.quote: The combinator collect will gather all values that are passed to it, and print out a histogram of these values.
quotes.location: §2.4 Monitoring Test Data, PDF page 3 (printed p. 270), left column, paragraph after the `classify` example — words 20

quotes.quote: The classify combinator does not change the meaning of a law, but it classifies some of the test cases
quotes.location: §2.4 Monitoring Test Data, PDF page 3 (printed p. 270), left column, directly under the `OK, passed 100 tests (43% trivial).` transcript — words 19; `classifies` is rendered as the fi ligature (image-checked)

quotes.quote: sized generates an a by passing the current size bound to its parameter
quotes.location: §3.2 Generators for User-Defined Types, PDF page 4 (printed p. 271), right column, under the `sized :: (Int -> Gen a) -> Gen a` declaration — words 13

quotes.quote: It is then up to the programmer to interpret the size bound in some reasonable way during test data generation.
quotes.location: §3.2 Generators for User-Defined Types, PDF page 4 (printed p. 271), right column, sentence following the quote above — words 20

quotes.quote: it seems to be very hard to construct a generator for a type, without knowing something about the desired distribution of test cases
quotes.location: §3.2 Generators for User-Defined Types, PDF page 4 (printed p. 271), left column, reason given for not generating `Arbitrary` instances automatically — words 23

quotes.quote: the false sense of security that can be engendered when one's program passes a large number of tests in trivial cases
quotes.location: §5.1.4 A False Sense of Security, PDF page 7 (printed p. 274), left column, first sentence of the section — words 21 (the full sentence begins `The most serious pitfall we uncovered with this experiment was ...` and exceeds 25 words)

quotes.quote: Our experience is that this results in far too high a proportion of trivial test cases, and therefore inefficient testing
quotes.location: §6.3 Test Data Generation, PDF page 10 (printed p. 277), left column, verdict on Maurer's grammar-leaf-probability generator — words 20; `inefficient` is rendered as the ffi ligature (control byte 0x0e, image-checked)

page_mapping: PDF page n = printed page 267+n (n=1 -> 268 ... n=12 -> 279), derived from Crossref `page: 268-279` and the 12-page carrier; the carrier itself prints no folios.

probe_observations.doi_landing: curl -sS -L https://doi.org/10.1145/351240.351266 -> 302 to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/351240.351266, then HTTP 403 (text/html, 5465 bytes). The DOI resolves; the publisher page does not serve article bytes to this host.
probe_observations.s182_row_claim: corpus SOURCES row S182 says `the article text was retrieved by DOI resolution on 2026-10-23`. As probed today a bare DOI resolution yields 403, so that line's retrieval route is not reproducible from this host without a browser/session; the row's quoted abstract string is nonetheless verbatim in this carrier (page 1 ABSTRACT, image-checked).
